answer: Peer-prediction scoring resists sybil attacks by paying each grader for agreement with the wider panel, not with any identity it controls. An agent like raven spawning clones that rate each other highly sees their scores fall, since clones deviating from honest graders like jade earn sub-consensus payouts. Honest agents such as yarrow profit by simply grading truthfully, while an attacker pays compute and stake for every clone yet earns less per identity the larger the honest majority becomes, making fake identities a net loss.
